conventions.convention: A weak action assigns F₁ literally equal to the identity and requires only existence of pairwise natural isomorphisms F_fg ≅ F_f F_g; no compositors or coherence are supplied.

Geometric intersection counts unmarked intersections with weight 1 and marked endpoints with weight 1/2; isotopic essential closed curves have exceptional value 2. Common boundary endpoints are resolved by pushing the first curve positively, so the extended function need not be symmetric.

The standard basic chain is b₀ from the boundary to q₀ and b_i from q_(i−1) to q_i for 1 ≤ i ≤ m. Positive braid generators are the preferred half twists about b_i. Nested twist τ_j encloses the suffix q_j,…,q_m.
The bigrading cover has fibre-generator monodromy (1,0) and positive puncture-generator monodromy (−2,1); preferred diffeomorphism lifts fix boundary tangent fibres. Only arcs admit bigradings.
In G(A_m), homological shift [1] acts by −1 and internal shift {1}, with M{r}_d = M_(d−r), acts by q. This is triangulated K₀ of bounded graded projective complexes, not short-exact-sequence G₀.
Decategorification uses coefficient columns in the vertex-projective basis; C[R_i]C⁻¹ equals the unreduced Burau generator with q=t and unchanged word order.

HHH uses R=Q[x₁−x₂,…,x_(m−1)−x_m], deg x_i=2, and unshifted B_i=R⊗_(R^s_i)R. A common trivial polynomial coordinate for products is t=(x₁+⋯+x_m)/m; the arbitrary coordinate x₁ does not generally act identically on the two bimodule sides.

The HHH positive generator is [R{2}→B_i] in degrees −1,0; the negative generator is [B_i{−2}→R{−2}] in degrees 0,1. Relative to the library Rouquier generators, invert every generator and add the writhe internal shift.
HHH is H^c(HH_h(R,F)), retaining (c,h,p); total Hochschild hyperhomology instead has total degree c−h and an induced filtration. The two constructions are not identified.

After the global KR correction (k,l)↦(k+1,l−1), the grading dictionary is k=−h, l=p−h, j=c. In raw KR indices, HHH^(c,h,p) corresponds to reduced H^(c,−h−1,p−h+1). Full a=0 specialization retains an extra zero Koszul row and two copies; recovering the original theory removes that row.

Reduced KR and the HHH comparison require a nonempty closure and at least one strand; the zero-strand tensor unit Q[a] is excluded. The Euler corollary uses the explicit v2 normalization, not the distinct published HOMFLYPT normalization.

Reductive and semisimple groups are smooth connected affine groups defined by trivial geometric unipotent radical and radical respectively. Over imperfect fields, trivial ground-field unipotent radical alone means pseudo-reductive.
R(G)=Z(G)_t is the largest central torus, not the possibly nonreduced neutral component of the centre. Finite intersections and central kernels may be infinitesimal.

Positive-root subgroup weight sets are quasi-closed using Chevalley coefficients nonzero in k. Ordinary root closure is equivalent only in characteristic 0 or p>3; smoothness is required in the root-group containment criterion.

Parabolic means a represented proper fppf quotient and permits nonsmooth subgroup schemes. The standard P_I classification and Levi decomposition are restricted to smooth parabolic subgroup varieties.
The opposite Gaussian big cell B⁻B is open dense; the longest Bruhat cell is its translate n_(w₀)(B⁻B), and the two open subsets are not asserted equal. Empty root systems are allowed, with B=G=T.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. For a split reductive pair (G,T), each root centralizer G_α is split reductive of semisimple rank one, with precisely the root spaces g_α and g_−α, each one-dimensional; rational multiples of α occurring as roots are only ±α. U_α≅G_a, and a smooth T-stable subgroup contains U_α iff its Lie algebra contains g_α. The rank-one Weyl reflection has its unique coroot and reflection formula. T and the root groups generate G; these give a reduced root datum and identify the Weyl group with its reflection group. Positive root groups multiply isomorphically onto B_u in any order, and smooth connected T-stable subgroup weight sets are exactly the stated quasi-closed subsets.

Assume AC. For all σ,τ∈B_(m+1), s₁,s₂∈Z and 0≤k,j≤m, Hom_(C_m)(R_τP_k,R_σP_j[s₁]{−s₂}) is free. Its rank Poincaré polynomial, weighted by q₁^s₁q₂^s₂, equals I^bigr(f̃_τb̃_k,f̃_σb̃_j); specialization q₁=q₂=1 gives twice the ordinary geometric intersection number.

Assume AC. The reduced resolution comparison carries χ₀ and χ₁ to rb_s and br_s up to nonzero rational units, intertwines the crossing cube after consistent vertex rescaling, and matches the displayed positive and corrected negative generator complexes. Removing the extra universal zero row recovers the original theory. After the global correction (k,l)↦(k+1,l−1), the grading correspondence is k=−h, l=p−h, j=c.

Assume AC. For a split reductive Borel pair (G,T,B), G is the disjoint union of smooth locally closed cells Bn_wB, and multiplication U^w×B→Bn_wB is an isomorphism. The flag cells are affine spaces of dimension n(w)=|Φ⁺∩wΦ⁻|. U⁻×T×U→G is an open immersion with dense image B⁻B, whose translate by n_(w₀) is the longest Bruhat cell. The k-point Bruhat decomposition holds, and diagonal G(k)-orbits on pairs of k-rational flags are indexed by W.

Assume AC. For smooth affine G and a cocharacter λ, P_G(λ), Z_G(λ), U_G(λ) are smooth subgroup schemes; P_G(λ)∩P_G(−λ)=Z_G(λ), U_G(λ) is normal, and U_G(λ)⋊Z_G(λ)→P_G(λ) is an isomorphism. U_G(−λ)×P_G(λ)→G is an open immersion; U_G(λ) is connected unipotent. Their Lie algebras are the nonnegative, zero and positive λ-weight spaces respectively. For reductive G, Z_G(λ) is reductive and R_u(P_G(λ))=U_G(λ).

Assume AC. For a split torus T acting by automorphisms on smooth connected affine G and every subsemigroup A⊆X(T), there is a unique smooth connected T-stable subgroup H_A whose Lie algebra is the sum of the weight spaces indexed by A∩Ψ. Every smooth connected T-stable subgroup with Lie algebra contained in that subspace lies in H_A. Positive rational multiples of a nonzero weight give the stated unipotent identity concentrator, with the smooth-subgroup containment criterion. Generated smooth connected T-stable subgroups have the semigroup generated by their Lie-weight semigroups.

For m≥1, choose a signed representative word t(β) for each β∈B_(m+1), with t(1) empty. Set F₁=Id and F_β=R_(t(β))⊗_(A_m)− for β≠1. These functors are equivalences and satisfy F_(βγ)≅F_βF_γ naturally. A finite sequence of presentation moves gives an explicit homotopy equivalence between word complexes; independence of that sequence and coherence are not asserted.

On [P₀],…,[P_m], [R_i][P_i]=−q[P_i], [R_i][P_(i+1)]=[P_(i+1)]−[P_i], [R_i][P_(i−1)]=[P_(i−1)]−q[P_i], and [R_i][P_j]=[P_j] for |i−j|>1, omitting nonexistent indices. The displayed invertible matrix C simultaneously satisfies C[R_i]C⁻¹=B_i at t=q, with the same generator indexing and word order.

For the displayed closed marked MOY resolution, the first rm layer relations, in the prescribed order, form a regular sequence in Q[x_(i,j)], with quotient B′(D), the unreduced balanced tensor product. Their Koszul complex resolves B′(D). The last m closure differences are excluded and are not generally regular.

For m≥1, every finitely generated graded projective left A_m-module is a finite direct sum of P_i{r}, with uniquely determined nonnegative multiplicities. The shifted vertex projectives are the indecomposable objects and their classes form a free abelian basis of the split Grothendieck group.
Assume AC. If a boundary-fixed mapping class f satisfies I(b_j,f(b_k))=I(b_j,f²(b_k))=I(b_j,b_k) for every 0≤j,k≤m, then [f]=1. Both iterates are required.

Assume AC. Subsets I⊆Δ classify the smooth parabolic subgroup varieties containing B, with P_I the union of Bruhat cells indexed by W_I and equivalently the dominant cocharacter limit group having zero simple pairings exactly on I. Its unipotent radical is the ordered product of positive root groups outside Φ_I, and U_I⋊L_I→P_I is a group-scheme isomorphism. Over an algebraically closed field every smooth parabolic is conjugate to a unique standard P_I. P_∅=B and P_Δ=G; nonsmooth proper-quotient parabolics are outside this classification.

concerns.concern: The page says, “A scalar computation in the one-object model shows that the pairwise isomorphisms of a weak action need not satisfy the pentagon.” The cited counterexample's Given explicitly uses “the category Q of complex vector spaces,” with scalar natural transformations of its identity functor. That category is not a one-object model. The scalar calculation itself supports the stated failure of automatic coherence.

seams_checked.note: The consumed block is [[1−t,t],[1,0]], acting on columns with the same word order. Vertex-coordinate row labels are reindexed from 1,…,m+1 to 0,…,m; the explicit C-conjugation uses q=t. The witness retains AC and the reduced/unreduced same-kernel qualification.

The arc/wide-edge rows, shifts, χ matrices and corrected negative χ₁-cone match. The consumer separates full a=0 doubling from the original reduced theory, derives reduced invariance rather than attributing it directly to the unreduced supplier, and retains AC and nonempty-closure restrictions.

The consumer explicitly inverts generators, translates (r)={−r}, accounts for the writhe shift and balanced-root unit, and specializes actual ambient homotopy identities using the common invariant coordinate. It cites the supplier's normalized canonical comparisons.

Rational representations are used with their comodule and all-algebra point meaning. GL(V) includes V=0. Finite-dimensional subcomodule and matrix-realization uses preserve the stated domains and choice assumptions.

Dual-number Lie spaces, base change, adjoint actions and injectivity for closed immersions are faithfully consumed. The page does not infer right exactness of Lie or identify a nonsmooth quotient's Lie algebra with a vector-space quotient.

Solvable splitting and Borel/tori conjugacy are applied over algebraic closures or within their explicit perfect-field hypotheses. Fixed-point arguments retain smooth connected solvable actors, complete nonempty schemes and AC. Multiplicative-type weight spaces retain arbitrary multiplicities.

Orbit and homogeneous-space uses retain smooth acting groups, separated finite-type targets, scheme-theoretic stabilizers and represented fppf quotients. Arbitrary closed subgroup schemes are allowed exactly where the supplier permits them; rational-point orbits are not substituted for quotient sheaves.

The opened consumer clauses preserve smoothness in Lie-generation tests, use the largest central torus Z(G)_t and finite possibly infinitesimal kernels, and consume the root-group coordinates, big-cell immersion, rational fundamental-weight vectors and standard maximal-parabolic clauses faithfully.

The coherent-action Definition explicitly fixes F₁=Id and adds chosen compositors and unit satisfying pentagon and unit triangles. Its weak-action citation preserves existence-only pairwise comparisons and does not infer coherence from them.
